bull_bear.body:
- Long-standing incumbency: manufacturing since 1966 and a stated 50 years presence in the electrical sector, cited by management as the basis for anticipated business potential
- Strong, well established distribution network, with new product variants added regularly through the same distribution channels
- In-house design and development centre equipped with required software, qualified engineers and the latest national and international standards; products designed using indigenous technology
- Continuous R&D that updates existing products and processes, improves quality and performance, makes products more cost-effective and upgrades them to the latest relevant standards
- Wide product range across electrical categories, allowing deeper penetration through existing channels
- Demonstrated capability in higher-rating equipment - 3,861 nos. of 66 kV rating Instrument Transformers supplied during the year, and manufacturing facilities revamped for MV indoor Instrument Transformers
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Severe competition and reduced demand in the electrical equipment market — Management states the Company has taken bold steps 'to remain competitive and to ensure survival by reducing cost and streamlining the overall operations process' and concedes 'severe competition and reduced demand', with optimism resting only on mid- and long-term prospects. Competitive intensity therefore bears directly on volumes and pricing.
- Availability and cost of funds — Explicitly flagged in MD&A: 'The availability and cost of the funds remain very important factors impacting on the plans of the Company and threatening the viability itself.' This is the one risk management raises to the level of a viability concern, and it constrains the ability to fund product expansion and working capital for the order book.
- Single-segment, single-business concentration — MD&A states segment-wise performance 'is not applicable to the Company as there is only one identified reportable segment'. All revenue depends on one electrical-equipment business with no diversifying cash flow, so a downturn in that market flows through undamped.
- Input availability and cost of critical materials — The cautionary statement names 'availability of critical materials and their cost' among the important factors that could influence operations, alongside 'domestic demand and supply conditions affecting selling prices' - i.e. input costs may not be passable into prices.
- New capacity additions by the industry and domestic demand/supply conditions affecting selling prices — Named in the cautionary statement as a factor influencing operations; industry capacity additions in a commoditising electrical-equipment market pressure realisations for a small manufacturer.
- Changes in government policies and tax laws — Named in the cautionary statement as a factor material to business operations. The Company's own outlook is explicitly premised on government structural reforms and initiatives (ease of doing business, Digital India, Make in India), so policy direction is a two-sided exposure.
- Dependence on promoter-group related parties for trade — Form AOC-2 discloses an ongoing sale/purchase/supply arrangement with Jyoti Limited, a Promoter Group Company, valued at Rs. 564.30 Lakhs for April 2025-March 2026, covering starters, motors, instrument transformers, control panels and spares, plus trade mark usage and service charges disclosed in the Ind AS 24 note. A material slice of trade and the brand right therefore sit with a promoter-group counterparty rather than at arm's length in the open market.
- Concentration in, and irrevocable reclassification of, the quoted equity investment in Jyoti Limited — The auditor's Emphasis of Matter records that management decided from 1 April 2025 to hold the quoted equity shares of Jyoti Limited for the long term, moving them from FVTPL to FVTOCI-NR under Ind AS 109 - a reclassification that 'cannot be revoked in future', with comparatives not restated. Reported fair market value on the reporting date was INR 527.67 lakhs and the change reduced income by INR 346.55 lakhs (gross) during the year. Reported earnings are thus exposed to, and now permanently insulated from, movements in a single promoter-group listed holding, and the ratio changes disclosed in MD&A are attributed to this same reclassification rather than to trading performance.
- Tax and duty disputes pending in appeal — Note 38 lists contingent liabilities not provided for, including 'Liabilities Disputed in appeals - Excise duty/Service Tax/Income Tax', alongside letters of credit, guarantees and counter guarantees. Adverse outcomes would crystallise as unprovided liabilities.
- Incomplete dematerialisation of promoter shareholding — The Secretarial Audit Report records the one exception to compliance: 'the shareholding of the promoters of the Company are not demated in full as per requirement of Regulation 31(2) of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015' - two individuals who had not converted their holdings have died and transmission has only been initiated. A standing listing-regulation non-compliance until transmission completes.

business.body: JSL Industries manufactures high-end electrical equipment - instrument transformers, LT switchboards and air circuit breakers, contactors and thermal overload relays, oil immersed starters, submersible pump controllers, motors and monoblock pumps - designed and developed in-house using indigenous technology and supplied to clients across India. The Company reports a single identified reportable segment, though the Board's Report and MD&A refer to an Instrument Transformer (IT) unit and a Motors and Pumps division. Products are supported by an in-house design and development centre with software, qualified engineers and current national and international standards, and by continuous R&D that updates existing products and processes.
business.title: What they do

business.body: - **Electrical equipment (single reportable segment):** Instrument Transformers, LT Switchboards, LT Air Circuit breakers, Contactors & Thermal overload relays, Oil Immersed Starters, Submersible pump controllers, TEFC/SPDP and VHS motors, Unibuilt mono-block pumps
business.title: Products & brands

business.body:
- Jyoti Limited — related party: Described in Form AOC-2 as a Promoter Group Company and listed under 'Other Related Parties' in the Ind AS 24 note. Dealings comprise sale/purchase/supply of goods and materials such as starters, motors, instrument transformers, control panels and spares, plus related services, service charges and trade mark usage; approved as a material arm's length contract by the Audit Committee, Board and shareholders at the 59th AGM. The Company also holds quoted equity shares of Jyoti Limited, reclassified to FVTOCI with effect from 1 April 2025 (auditor's Emphasis of Matter).
- Insutech Industries Limited — related party: Described in Form AOC-2 as a Promoter Group Company and listed under 'Other Related Parties' in the Ind AS 24 note. Arrangement covers sale/purchase/supply of goods and materials such as starters, motors, instrument transformers, control panels and spares and related services; approved by the Audit Committee and Board on 25 March 2025.

outlook.body:
- Remain competitive by reducing cost and streamlining the overall operations process
- Deepen penetration into the market for existing products and continue focus on product expansion, adding new product variants through the same distribution channels
- Sustain continuous R&D to update existing products and processes, improve quality and performance, make products more cost-effective and upgrade them to the latest relevant standards

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The bundle discloses no new plant, no capacity addition and no dated expansion project. The only physical-asset actions management describes are incremental upgrades to the existing footprint: manufacturing facilities for MV indoor Instrument Transformers have been revamped, and Energy Efficient Motors have been developed to IS 12615:2011. Forward intent is commercial rather than capital - deepening market penetration, continuing product expansion with new variants through the existing distribution channels, and an added / improved product range in the IT & Motor Unit - supported by an in-house design and development centre. Management notes that the availability and cost of funds remain very important factors impacting the Company's plans.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Demand for electrical products is expected to grow; electrical equipment manufacturing is described as a very important sector for a developing country like India, making the long-term outlook bright
- With the added / improved range of products in the IT & Motor Unit, management expects better growth prospects
- Management expects to increase the volume of business in the current year, barring unforeseen circumstances
- A pending order book, with further orders in the pipeline, is expected to contribute substantially to turnover and profitability during 2026-27
- Motors and Pumps division performance is described as good, with a better divisional outlook and good business expected for motors in FY 2026-27
- Macro backdrop: the IMF maintained India's GDP growth forecast at 6.5% for both FY2026 and FY2027, supported by strong private consumption, particularly rural, and substantial public infrastructure investment
- Government initiatives - ease of doing business, Digital India, Make in India, Start up - cited as reasons the industry is hopeful for a brighter future
- Headwinds: severe competition and reduced demand, though optimism about mid- and long-term growth prospects remains
- Availability and cost of funds remain very important factors impacting the Company's plans
- Cautionary statement names domestic demand and supply conditions affecting selling prices, new capacity additions, availability and cost of critical materials, and changes in government policies and tax laws as the factors that could influence operations
- Pending orders worth Rs. 2671.76 Lacs on hand, with further orders in the pipeline, to be executed to provide substantial contribution to turnover and profitability during 2026-27

sk.overview: Powerica operates across two industries: (1) India's standby power / diesel-generator (DG set) market, where DG sets, UPS, inverters and battery storage provide backup power during outages/voltage fluctuations across commercial, manufacturing, IT/data-centre, telecom and infrastructure sectors (F&S Report); and (2) India's wind power sector within the broader renewable energy industry, where wind plays a pivotal role in the country's energy transition (CRISIL Report).
